title: Real-time Telemetry Stream Processing for Smart Grids
business: Utility companies managing distributed energy resources and smart grid infrastructure.
problem: Legacy relational databases struggle to ingest high-frequency sensor telemetry, leading to write contention and delayed visibility into grid stability.
solution: Valkey Streams provide a lightweight, append-only log structure that decouples data ingestion from downstream analytical processing, while optional persistence ensures data durability during maintenance cycles.
steps: Initialize a Valkey Stream to act as the primary ingestion buffer for incoming sensor telemetry packets.
Use XADD to append incoming sensor readings to the stream, assigning unique entry IDs for chronological ordering.
Configure Append Only File (AOF) persistence to ensure that telemetry logs are flushed to disk, preventing data loss during unexpected restarts.
Implement consumer groups using XREADGROUP to allow multiple analytical services to process the telemetry stream concurrently without duplicate work.
outcome: The utility company achieves consistent, low-latency ingestion of grid data, enabling near-instantaneous detection of load imbalances across the network.
limitation: Because Valkey operates primarily in-memory, the dataset size is constrained by available RAM; monitor the memory usage via the INFO memory command to prevent eviction of critical stream data.

diagram.title: Telemetry Stream Ingestion Flow
diagram.description: This diagram illustrates how sensor data flows from the grid into the Valkey stream and is subsequently consumed by analytical services.

code.content:
# Add a sensor reading to the stream
XADD grid-telemetry * sensor_id 101 voltage 230.5
# Read new entries as part of a consumer group
XREADGROUP GROUP group1 consumer1 STREAMS grid-telemetry >
code.explanation: The XADD command appends the sensor data to the stream, while XREADGROUP allows the analytical service to consume the stream reliably.

questions.question: In Real-time Telemetry Stream Processing for Smart Grids, why is Valkey preferred over a traditional relational database for ingestion?
options: It eliminates write contention by using an append-only log structure for high-frequency data.
It provides infinite storage capacity for historical telemetry data.
It automatically converts telemetry data into relational tables.
It requires no configuration for data persistence.
questions.explanation: Valkey Streams act as an append-only log, which is optimized for high-frequency ingestion compared to relational databases that suffer from write contention.
questions.evidence: Valkey Streams provide a lightweight, append-only log structure that decouples data ingestion from downstream analytical processing, while optional persistence ensures data durability during maintenance cycles.

questions.question: In Real-time Telemetry Stream Processing for Smart Grids, what is a primary limitation of the implementation?
options: The system cannot handle multiple consumer groups.
The system is limited by available RAM, requiring monitoring to prevent data eviction.
The system does not support disk-based persistence.
The system is incompatible with AOF logging.
questions.explanation: Since Valkey is an in-memory store, memory capacity is a hard constraint that must be monitored to avoid accidental data loss via eviction.
questions.evidence: Because Valkey operates primarily in-memory, the dataset size is constrained by available RAM; monitor the memory usage via the INFO memory command to prevent eviction of critical stream data.
